name: Koine Greek Possession (Acts of the Apostles)
summary: PKD reports being able to read passages of *Acts of the Apostles* in Koine Greek — a language he had no formal training in — during a brief altered state in March 1974, and recognizing that the historical setting of *Acts* (first-century Mediterranean) is the underlying real time.
description: PKD reports that in March 1974, during the period of the pink-beam transmission, he found himself able to read Koine Greek text from the Greek New Testament — specifically passages from *The Acts of the Apostles* — and to comprehend it directly without translation. He had had limited Latin study but no Greek. The episode is the seed of his subsequent claim that 1974 California is a stage-managed simulation overlaid on first-century Rome.

pkd_interpretations.interpretation: I am remembering Koine Greek from a first-century life in which I was a Christian named Thomas.
The first-century Christian Thomas is occupying me; I am his temporal continuation.
The Greek letters were numbers being transformed into letters and back, exhibiting structures I later learned were called gematria.

scholar_interpretations.interpretation: McKee places the Koine Greek vision within an early-Christian-mystical lineage (the Pentecost gift of tongues, gnostic Sophia, etc.).

primary_sources.excerpt: Multiple segments describe the Koine Greek experience.

primary_quote: I had had limited Latin and no Greek; yet I was reading the Acts of the Apostles in Koine Greek and understanding it directly.
pkd_doubt_evidence: PKD acknowledges he cannot prove the comprehension; no witness was present.
